chunks: What is LiDAR. The question: What is LiDAR?
LiDAR stands for Light Detection And Ranging.
It is a sensor that fires short pulses of invisible infrared laser light and times how long each pulse takes to bounce off an object and return.
Since the speed of light is known, that time gives the distance. Aim the laser in many directions and you get a 3D map of the surroundings.
Shout in a canyon and time the echo. The speed of sound times half the echo time is the distance to the wall. LiDAR does the same with light.
Light is about a million times faster than sound, so the timing has to be far finer: a nanosecond, one billionth of a second, is already 0. 3 m of light travel.
The canyon picture also lacks something: LiDAR sends its own light, so it works in the dark.
The controller fires the laser and starts a clock. The return passes through a narrow band-pass filter (to reject sunlight), the detector and TIA, and stops the clock at the TDC.
The scanner decides in which direction each pulse points.
Time of flight: the time a pulse takes to go out and come back. Distance is the speed of light times that time, divided by two.
Pulse: a very short burst of light, a few nanoseconds long. Active sensor: a sensor that sends out its own signal instead of using ambient light.
Scanning: pointing the laser in many directions, by spinning, steering mirrors or flashing the whole scene. Point cloud: the output, a set of 3D points with a position for each.
A pulse leaves the sensor and returns 200 nanoseconds later. Light covers about 0. 3 m per nanosecond, so in 200 nanoseconds it travels 60 m.
That is out and back, so the target is half of that: 30 m away. Repeat in many directions, and each return gives one point in space. Together they form a point cloud.
That is the whole idea.
"LiDAR is Light Detection And Ranging: an active sensor that fires laser pulses and times how long they take to come back.
Distance is c times the round-trip time over two, so 200 nanoseconds is 30 meters.
By steering the beam, with a spinning head, MEMS mirror or flash illumination, it builds a 3D point cloud of the scene.
It gives accurate geometry in any lighting, but has lower resolution than a camera and no color."
